title: Venus and the Cat
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Cat fell in love with a handsome young man, and begged the goddess Venus to change her into a woman. Venus was very gracious about it, and changed her at once into a beautiful maiden, whom the young man fell in love with at first sight and shortly afterwards married.

One day Venus thought she would like to see whether the Cat had changed her habits as well as her form; so she let a mouse run loose in the room where they were. Forgetting everything, the young woman had no sooner seen the mouse than up she jumped and was after it like a shot: at which the goddess was so disgusted that she changed her back again into a Cat.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Cat beg Venus to do?
options: Give her the young man's love directly
Make the young man immortal
Change her into a woman
Teach her how to speak

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does Venus respond to the Cat's request?
options: She is gracious and changes her at once into a beautiful maiden
She refuses, saying cats cannot become human
She agrees only on the condition that the Cat never chases mice again
She asks the young man for his permission first

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens between the young man and the transformed Cat?
options: He is suspicious of her from the very start
He refuses to meet her despite Venus's efforts
He marries someone else instead
He falls in love with her at first sight and marries her

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Venus want to test one day?
options: Whether the young man still loved his wife
Whether the Cat had changed her habits as well as her form
Whether the Cat could still speak her original language
Whether the marriage would last a full year

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Venus let loose in the room to test the transformed Cat?
options: A small bird
A ball of yarn
A mouse
A basket of fish

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the young woman do the moment she sees the mouse?
options: She jumps up and is after it like a shot
She screams and runs from the room
She calmly picks it up and sets it free
She calls for her husband to catch it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Venus do after seeing the woman chase the mouse?
options: She scolds her but allows her to remain human
She asks the young man to forgive his wife
She removes the mouse and says nothing more
She changes her back again into a Cat

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Venus decide to test the Cat rather than simply trust the transformation?
options: She wants to see if the young man still loves his wife
She suspects that changing appearance does not necessarily change deeper instincts
She wants an excuse to reverse a decision she regrets
She is bored and looking for entertainment

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "gracious" mean in "Venus was very gracious about it"?
options: Suspicious and reluctant
Confused and uncertain
Kind and willing to help
Angry and offended

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: A change in outward form does not necessarily change one's underlying instincts
Goddesses should never grant wishes to animals
Marriages between different kinds of creatures cannot succeed
Mice are more tempting to cats than any other creature

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Cat first want to become a woman?
options: She wants to escape a life of being hunted
She wants to live inside a warm house
She is curious about human customs
She has fallen in love with a handsome young man

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how quickly does the young man fall in love with the transformed Cat?
options: Only after many months
At first sight
After a long courtship
Only once she proved herself trustworthy

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the young woman forget the moment she sees the mouse?
options: Her husband's name
Her manners at the table
Everything
Her promise to Venus

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the phrase "like a shot" suggest about the woman's reaction to the mouse?
options: It was instant and instinctive, without any thought at all
It was slow and carefully considered
It was performed only to please her husband
It was staged to test Venus's reaction

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is Venus "disgusted" rather than simply amused by what she sees?
options: It shows that the young man no longer loves his wife
It reveals that the mouse was actually another disguised creature
It proves that the marriage was a mistake from the beginning
It confirms that her gift of transformation did not truly change the Cat's nature

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "maiden" mean in "a beautiful maiden"?
options: A goddess in disguise
A young woman
A servant in a household
A skilled dancer

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Cat marries a young man and lives happily ever after as a woman
Venus refuses to ever grant the Cat's wish
A Cat turned into a woman reveals her true nature by chasing a mouse, so Venus undoes the change
The young man discovers his wife was once a cat and leaves her
